newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - ADRs ease along with dollar.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - ADRs ease along with dollar.

text.p: American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) largely eased along with the rest of the New York markets on Friday, hurt by a weaker dollar and options expirations, traders said.
"The U.S. stocks are weaker so everything is up for sale today," a trader said.
European ADRs were mostly lower in featureless trade as a weakening dollar hurt prospects for blue-chip exporters. Most European markets were closed for the Assumption Day holiday, limiting activity.
A trader said the fall in ADRs was likely to steepen later Friday amid options expirations. "Basically, it's a waiting game for the options, and activity is being driven by program trading," he said.

British Sky Broadcasting Group Plc dropped 2-1/4 to 42-1/2, a 12-month low, after the satellite TV broadcaster reported full-year profits at the lower end of analysts' expectations. Dutch electronics company Philips Electronics NV fell 2-7/16 to 73-3/16.
Chinese ADRs dropped overall, hit by profit-taking and an overnight fall in the Hong Kong stock market.
"This week they traded up a lot, and it's an overall weaker market," a trader said, noting that the Chinese exchanges have risen 50 percent in the last two months.

Shanghai Petrochemical Co Ltd fell four to 34-3/4 and Beijing Yanhua Petrochemical Co Ltd dropped two to 17-7/8. Jilin Chemical Industrial Co fell 2-15/16 to 27-3/4 and China East Airlines Corp Ltd was off 3-1/2 to 29.
All four companies were among the percentage loss leaders on the New York Stock Exchange.
Among other Asian ADRs, Indonesian telephone company PT Telkom dropped 1-7/8 to 24-1/2 and Indonesia Satellite Satellite Corp fell 1-2/16 to 24-11/16.
A trader said the ADRs were hit by a "double whammy" -- a plunge in the value of the rupiah and a record one-day drop in the Jakarta stock market.
Among Latin American ADRs, Telefonos de Mexico fell 3/16 to 51-15/16. Mexican broadcaster TV Azteca was scheduled to launch its initial public offering on Friday.
ADRs allow U.S. trade of foreign shares.
